title: Values and loops in C
summary: Compile a small C program that branches and iterates over an array.

scenario.briefing: A robotics log stores sensor changes as integers. Count the positive changes in C without reading past the array.

objectives.description: Apply the taught syntax in a working file.

hints: The loop already has the correct bound.
Test the current element before incrementing.
Place count += 1 inside an if block.

misconceptions.description: Assuming sizeof inside the function returns the array length.
misconceptions.feedback: Inside the function the parameter is a pointer, so sizeof gives the pointer size. Pass the length explicitly.

misconceptions.testDescription: The loop reads each value and counts only positives.
misconceptions.feedback: count += 0 never changes the count. Increment only in the positive branch.

sections.title: C values and decisions
sections.body: C declares values with a type and storage duration: int count = 3; double price = 12.50; char grade = 'A';. int, double, char, and pointers are distinct types. A string is a pointer to a null-terminated array of char. An if statement selects a branch, and a switch selects among integer cases. A for loop uses an index and an explicit bound: for (int index = 0; index < length; index += 1) { ... }.

steps.title: Count positive sensor changes
steps.prompt: Edit main.c. count_positive receives a pointer and a length and returns how many values are greater than zero.

tests.description: The function keeps the pointer-and-length signature.
The loop reads each value and counts only positives.

hints: The loop bound is already correct.
Increment only inside the positive branch.

localVerification.description: Compile main.c with warnings treated as errors using the C compiler.

steps.title: Check the semantics

statements.label: An array passed to a function arrives as a pointer to its first element.
C checks array bounds automatically on every access.
Passing the length separately lets the function honor the real bound.
A null-terminated string stores its length in a separate field.

steps.explanation: C does not carry array length with a pointer. The caller and callee must agree on the bound.
hints: C does not check array bounds.
A pointer does not carry the array length.
